We have been talking a lot on the market looking for demand and it’s exactly what is happening. Basis and futures both weak on corn and beans as SAM sold all the Oct-Jan corn as US futures ran up. Beans China is a smaller PNW buyer than market thought and selling a bean train Oct-Dec next to impossible. Corn same for the most part. We need to see demand or basis snuggles more. We are out of harms way and will now dump and ship. Open today 8-7 in line by 6.30. Sunday 12-7 in line by 6.30. Monday we start to pile.

Traders have opinions as does everyone. Be careful on opinions. I am asked often my thoughts on reports but the one who has all the tools is USDA and is why they drive the market. We watch what demand does on rallies and price drops as that is a great opinion. As a producer you have to to look when cash needs are, profit levels are, when can you haul, carries etc and lock in prices. We do not sell when we know very bullish items but even then have a finger on avg sell button. Just a thought on USDA reports. We did see some nibbles on corn and beans on this price drop.If you are a Co-op customer and want our paid for Van Trump report call me or Chris. I really like his way of selling and reporting.

After reading a lot of info USDA in the past is very slow to adjust yield data from Oct very quickly. Funds are long which in beans and corn is a risk of them selling. We are well sold but we would suggest to raise cash sell all the beans. Hold wheat thats left. And keep corn for a better basis and carry. Just a thought. Open today for beans only 12-7 All stations. Call 218-791-5769 for hedging tonight.

Markets slip a little as so much world pressure to end the wars comes at UN. In corn and wheat we priced ourselves out of the world market on last run up so a lot hinges on US/China making a sweat ag deal. New crop sales are slow for wheat and corn. One thing we know is corn basis is weak( advise setting old crop) as bins are cleaned and exports slow. Sept see's exports switch to beans which takes up the freight and export loading's. Great night last night at the meeting and it marked my 40th annual meeting and I was given a a signed pic of the first 8500 shuttle( first in the US) we did by the staff. The board also took part and overall I was surprised and touched by it. Its been my honor to have served as GM for 40 plus years and to train and see the next generation take over has been great. I am not done but for sure have slowed a bit. My advise to all the younger farmers is do the best job of production you can but keep selling profit levels when they come and do not swing for the fence. It is so much better to just keep selling the profitable levels and out the curve to build prices. careful to listen to all the noise. Wheat and beans only today as we are full of corn. Closing at two today.

Markets had a rough week with US weather looking good and markets realizing the size of carry outs still to deal with. Producer also was very active seller weeks ago on rally filling pipeline. No buying as of yet from China and SAM crop looking good. Seasonal rules for grains has not Changed. If no weather issues wheat is sold by May 18th, corn July 1 and beans end of summer. You can always sell and buy options if want upside protection. Once again scale in selling was best. Selling carries and building a price. Just so much risk in today's world and with funds markets move higher and lower than should. When I was told as a very young trader a older wiser trader told me the market really does not care about my issues and it holds no survivors. Learned that one a time or two. It is all about managing risk which takes staying in tune with the market, planing space and money needs ahead of actual need. One thing we know there will in time be another rally. Have a great weekend. Call 218-791-5769 if you just want to visit on markets.

It was great see everyone last night and hope you got a lot from it and felt appreciated. We greatly appreciate the chance to assist in good and hard times. I believe Rob was a great fit and very informed as he is very connected. Not a futures broker or market advisor. He is UGC's futures guy and see's cash trading vs futures all over the world. He was on loan from UGC's Pres Augusto. That said I have always had the belief Honeyford needs to have direct unfiltered info and market bids.We have spent a lot( a life time) of years developing this and am still looking to get closer to the end user. Most co-ops and big grain the news is going through trade desks and they do know know the people selling the grain. We do. We deal direct with the exporter and end user and I believe we have info very few co will pass along. Think how many times we write or talk on something then its news. Along with this we have built a delivery system that connects you to end users all over the world. Our goal is to help you not pick you off.

Markets in corn and wheat are gaining sales by the day. Good stuff and needed. We believe beans will have a export time and crush time so we will be loading our first train to Mexico and the binning and holding the rest.

Rob talked last night of building a price. How many times have we said that. all the time. Its always a need in good prices or poor. Ask Wade for more details and plans. Call me anytime to visit. 218-791-5769.

I want to say hats off to everyone for the job of marketing a lower priced crop. We sold last spring, sold basis Nov,Dec and Jan in a big way way then sold futures old and new on this last rally. This was for wheat and corn. Beans you sold last spring and balance this past few months. Building a price via carries and selling basis to match is best. Second is selling a good basis then setting futures within time period basis is set. This is more risky as you are subject to futures. I like selling futures way ahead and then having time to set basis. Wheat only today as we are full of corn until a train Sunday.In line by two as I am sending train crew home just after two. SAM weather is good and no other news. Tariff talk is quiet today. Also thanks to everyone for pounding in the contracts. Most are in or very close. FYI watch bin tops as we are seeing a lot of issues. Please advise us on bins that are possible issues and we will work with you. Please do not try to blend off in bottoms as when we are loading trains it may come through as a slug and create a real issue. Have a great weekend!!! Enjoy the warm weather.

I do talk a lot about basis and getting it right but getting futures and cash sold at a avg decent price is more important. Be careful not to get hung up on basis contracting only or who is paying a few penny's more. I have seen it to many times were great basis sales roll and turn into poor ones. Also futures move around way more than basis and getting them sold out the curve is so so important. IE selling new crop ahead and watching basis is good. Building a new crop cash that works. And there are times to sell basis but point is just to think basis is not best. Sometimes you miss the rally. It is also so so hard to hit the top so avg scale in is safest. Look at fundamentals but of course but listen to guys like Van Trump and his marketing. Its never about going for the fence. Its selling in a timeline for profit. Anyways lots of moving parts and marketing needs your time being spent daily on it. Any help you need please please call. Wade and myself for sure can walk through the markets. With the wind today we are closing at 3. in line by 2.30. Next week to help get grain off the farm to town we will be open 7.30-6 at Honeyford two pits for corn and one wheat.

It was a very busy week. Futures run up brought out selling. Warm weather brought out haulers so pipelines are stocked. This is why on a non short crop year it works well to sell basis ahead when futures are lower and few are selling. Then on a futures rally you hit them. Or sell futures out the curve is really best and set basis on time periods were selling cash is light. Both work but generally selling cash on a futures run up you leave a little on the table. We liked selling 4.75 Dec corn futures and then rolling them out the curve later to build 5.00 plus futures price. Then hitting a -50 basis next winter for 4.50 cash. Wheat same strategy works. Its all about risk management and building a cash price. All basis levels this week are unchanged and we hit our target futures to trigger sales. Call to visit on markets.

For decades I have said and advised the same thing. Building a price is best and simple. In carry markets which are most times it is best to look at the range the futures have carved out and sell in the top portion. Then sell the carry and in most cases leaving the basis open. Then as demand comes in for your delivery period hit the basis. In most years the front end futures price drops to the same range as the carry month. Thus making basis contracting out the curve not a solid plan. Better to lock in the futures carry then assign a basis to that sale. Plus it is NOT about hitting home runs its about consistent selling at decent levels. With harvest behind us there is zero sell pressure on the market. Russia is pushing which is adding in some risk prem to the market. Weather world wide is a neg as it is good. Only crop I see selling right now (as we have solid others recently) is beans. Our last bean train is Jan 5th-8th. I think you just cash then in and move onto next year. Remember its basis roll time for Dec contracts.

We have been talking and advising selling the carry on rallies. There is nothing very bullish today unless SA weather provides. Earning the carry in large carryout markets is hard. Meaning front end price a lot of the time turns into the back end price when we get there. Or something close. I prefer using grain bins to sell cash carries not hold cash grain. Remember Ed Usset program on building a price. Ron Olson VP General Mills always schooled us in the market is talking. Are we listening??? He also said the price bathtub always equalizes. Just a couple things that stuck with me. We look at export basis/ domestic demand every day vs futures and carries to decide on a plan for space. I would highly advise you do the same as long term price building. Anything you need is these areas contact Wade or myself to make a plan.

This week selling off continued as managed money sold wheat and beans to the short side with corn flat. Fundamentals on wheat were North America weather, India announcing little imports, Ukraine raising crop est and harvest. Basis levels were mostly unchanged. Spreads did widen as 2023 crop gets dumped and sold against the July making room for the new crop. Once again the avg in sales has worked ( bird in the hand thing) as most spring rallies fail. Wheat rallies in mid May then sells off into harvest and then rallies in Nov/Dec. A weather issue or a surprise in end of the month acre report is needed to really turn the market. But it is summer and weather is weather. Need corn next week as the late spring and seady flow of trains has us running low on bu. Please help us out on contracted grain by delivering as much as possible.

We rolled to Sept on corn and are still looking for a few bu for last summer train. In by August 10th. Markets have digested the crop conditions ( solid) and SAM crop reduction along with Black Sea reduction and has quieted down. Basis wise it was quiet this week on all crops. All are a bit on the weak side but commercial is mostly handling it. Futures in wheat and corn were weak as they see planting windows. Now its next weeks planting progress late Monday and weather that will move the market. If long range weather forecasts are correct May stays wet and then turns dryer in June. Western Canada would suffer from this as moisture would not flow that far north. Now gulf moisture is making its way to Canada as well. Would great for us as we have subsoil and with normal rains there is real possibilities yield wise. As always if you get undersold or oversold short date cheap options are the way to go. Marketing is all about building a price not trying to extract it via getting a extra few cents at time of sale. It may make you feel like you won but the true win is when you sell carry and rallies. Then taking a wait approach to setting the basis. We are here to assist in pointing out opportunities and making plans. Bins are built to earn money and is best if carrying sold grain for the carry.

Taran Langland 

Grew up in Enderlin, ND and moved to Grand Forks after college where I my married my wife, who is from the Fordville area. We have a 2.5 year old daughter, another baby due in May, and a 3 year old Golden Retriever. My background in Ag is with a seed company as a territory manager and in the digital ag space as a field technology specialist. I’m excited to work for Honeyford Famers Elevator and I look forward to working with you and making your operation as successful as possible.


Max Schlosser.

I grew up in central North Dakota just about my whole life, more specifically in Rugby. My father was an agronomist, and my mother’s side of the family farmed near my hometown. I have always enjoyed agriculture as well as everything else outdoors, so I went on to study agronomy at Bismarck State College. After my first year their; I spent my spring and summer as an intern with an agronomy center close to home. I then went on to finish college up this past year. I am now here very eager to meet and work with all of the local farmers in the area.

Overnights super quiet as USDA report is Friday. It is a big one. The last rally gave us great opportunity to hedge more grain and that we did. We had a week of steady calls selling grains. Why is we see and live the demand side of the market and were demand is so will prices go. Money flows in and out but fundamentals in time RULE! Well we see Brazil selling the corn and beans through Nov and then again in Feb. We have about the normal row crop business this fall than we normally have. That is a big deal if we produce a crop. That was our reason for being so vocal on selling. Now if we get back to having supplies enough to export prices will drop to find demand. As of today that is still below current prices by a bit.


Markets now will need to see rains, demand happen and USDA report for direction.


We will be closing Friday at 1.30 for a long weekend. I will be your trader 218-791-5769 if you need assistance.


Have a great long weekend!

This was why we recommended scale up selling into this market as we see the demand side.


That said makes overnight In our opinion keep looking at demand and forecast. If they move rains into 3-5 day forecast it likely drops more. If its a pattern change and rains they est new yield and were demand steps back in and go there.

Report day is the 12th and history has this one a market mover. We have posted recently defending 8 dollar wheat and actually if behind on sales of corn and beans buy short date puts or sell more cash or both. last report we bought short date puts and it rallied and gave us a selling opportunity but lost some on puts. That's ok and what the move is designed to do. Rule of thumb is sell balance of old crop wheat by May 12th, Corn by July 1st and beans late July mid August. But this year we have the inverses to contend with so it's harder.


Morning weather looks like less rain and warm and dry after this weekend giving the north country time to plant most if not all of its crops. Soil if in great shape and subsoil best in aa while. This should get plants out of the ground and growing in a hurry saving its vigor.


World markets are cheaper than US so we do have downside potential. Bean demand is down from China and Brazil has a big crop. Corn same. Wheat its Australia, Canada and Black Sea.


Long term its weather and Russia/Ukraine as what if's.

One thing we know is corn basis is weak( advise setting old crop) as bins are cleaned and exports slow. Sept see's exports switch to beans which takes up the freight and export loading's. Great night last night at the meeting and it marked my 40th annual meeting and I was given a a signed pic of the first 8500 shuttle( first in the US) we did by the staff. The board also took part and overall I was surprised and touched by it. Its been my honor to have served as GM for 40 plus years and to train and see the next generation take over has been great. I am not done but for sure have slowed a bit. My advise to all the younger farmers is do the best job of production you can but keep selling profit levels when they come and do not swing for the fence. Markets had a rough week with US weather looking good and markets realizing the size of carry outs still to deal with. Producer also was very active seller weeks ago on rally filling pipeline. No buying as of yet from China and SAM crop looking good. Seasonal rules for grains has not Changed. If no weather issues wheat is sold by May 18th, corn July 1 and beans end of summer. You can always sell and buy options if want upside protection. Once again scale in selling was best. Selling carries and building a price. Just so much risk in today's world and with funds markets move higher and lower than should. When I was told as a very young trader a older wiser trader told me the market really does not care about my issues and it holds no survivors. Learned that one a time or two. It is all about managing risk which takes staying in tune with the market, planing space and money needs ahead of actual need. One thing we know there will in time be another rally. Have a great weekend. Call 218-791-5769 if you just want to visit on markets.

More details come out of the grain part of the China deal and mostly it was for beans. Amounts were spelled out. 12MMT this Year and 25 next three which is back to high end in recent history. No mention of corn or wheat. Sorghum was mentioned but no amounts so everything but beans will be price driven. But for corn we have a solid export base with new trade deals in Asia so China business would just be extra. So far no offers on boats from China on beans except those sold before trade deal. Market is holding its breath but do not get to bulled up as this amount( even if bought) is half for this year. Scale in sales. Stay on track selling corn. We sold 4.30/4.35 Dec 2025 or best carry and sold Dec 2026. We believe overall by binning and catching rallies we have done ok. Add that with early sales and for sure ok. On Corn if short space ( everyone is)sell and buys calls. Commercial DP costs rarely net out at the end of the day. Thanks

Along with this we have built a delivery system that connects you to end users all over the world. Our goal is to help you not pick you off.

31st at 6 is the annual report, 6.30 guest speaker Rob Froom from UGC will talk on the world markets and trade deals etc. A MUST see! I have a lot to say so read close. Weather remains really good for finishing row crops. If holding old crop and need the space clear it now while there is room before harvest cranks up. It looks to be a big one. Basis levels in wheat will reset once we see pro and quality but this week alone we seen a 10-20 drop. I see pro prem quickly drop as 15 pro weakens sharply. If holding cash corn its time to clear the bins and move on. Beans also. We need a China trade deal soon or bean basis is going to get smoked! If next week when US / China meet and tariffs are put off then we likely miss our Oct ship time frame for beans. Thus few harvest homes. Thus wide basis. I would look to bin and haul in Dec/Jan when we likely do bean trains( assuming Oct does not work out). Corn exports remain very good and is what we will ship if no bean program. Time will tell. Point is clean every bin you got and plan for worst. Marketing this year will be using the wide carries to enhance sales. Building a price like we say. Do not use basis contracts in this structure. In line by 2 today. Just got done with a train and closing at 2. Call me at 218-791--5769 to discuss above comments.

Corn continues to drift lower on what looks to be a very large US crop on top of a very large SAM crop. I am and have been for some time concerned how under sold the world farmer is. I have talked to counterparts in Canada and who know SAM well and everyone is undersold. End user is in no hurry to cover as every day its cheaper but this cheap price will increase demand. Wheat sold off hard as finishing rains have happened the last week. Some dry spots in west, MT and Canada but with harvest underway and a good HRW crop 5.40-6.00 cash seems to be the range for now. Bean market is waiting for August weather and China but is setting up to move lower if rains come and no large China program. Basis also gets crushed at harvest if China does not buy Sept/Oct. Real possibility. Overall bin space will be a big issue. I would look at temp strg for beans and corn. There will be export programs for all crops and good demand but logistics take time. if you have some old crop corn we can load a late July/ August train so you need to have bins empty. Actually all bins need to be empty of all crops with temps lined up. If you want to visit call 218-791-5769 for more inside thoughts. Monday taking all crops.

I do talk a lot about basis and getting it right but getting futures and cash sold at a avg decent price is more important. Be careful not to get hung up on basis contracting only or who is paying a few penny's more. I have seen it to many times were great basis sales roll and turn into poor ones. Also futures move around way more than basis and getting them sold out the curve is so so important. IE selling new crop ahead and watching basis is good. Building a new crop cash that works. And there are times to sell basis but point is just to think basis is not best. Sometimes you miss the rally. It is also so so hard to hit the top so avg scale in is safest. Look at fundamentals but of course but listen to guys like Van Trump and his marketing. Its never about going for the fence. Its selling in a timeline for profit. Anyways lots of moving parts and marketing needs your time being spent daily on it. Any help you need please please call. Wade and myself for sure can walk through the markets. With the wind today we are closing at 3. in line by 2.30. Next week to help get grain off the farm to town we will be open 7.30-6 at Honeyford two pits for corn and one wheat.

It was a very busy week. Futures run up brought out selling. Warm weather brought out haulers so pipelines are stocked. This is why on a non short crop year it works well to sell basis ahead when futures are lower and few are selling. Then on a futures rally you hit them. Or sell futures out the curve is really best and set basis on time periods were selling cash is light. Both work but generally selling cash on a futures run up you leave a little on the table. We liked selling 4.75 Dec corn futures and then rolling them out the curve later to build 5.00 plus futures price. Then hitting a -50 basis next winter for 4.50 cash. Wheat same strategy works. Its all about risk management and building a cash price. All basis levels this week are unchanged and we hit our target futures to trigger sales. Call to visit on markets.

For decades I have said and advised the same thing. Building a price is best and simple. In carry markets which are most times it is best to look at the range the futures have carved out and sell in the top portion. Then sell the carry and in most cases leaving the basis open. Then as demand comes in for your delivery period hit the basis. In most years the front end futures price drops to the same range as the carry month. Thus making basis contracting out the curve not a solid plan. Better to lock in the futures carry then assign a basis to that sale. Plus it is NOT about hitting home runs its about consistent selling at decent levels. With harvest behind us there is zero sell pressure on the market. Russia is pushing which is adding in some risk prem to the market. Weather world wide is a neg as it is good. Only crop I see selling right now (as we have solid others recently) is beans. Our last bean train is Jan 5th-8th. I think you just cash then in and move onto next year. Remember its basis roll time for Dec contracts.

Important: In a effort to get a wheat bin flipped to corn we staggered a wet corn semi then loaded a outbound wheat semi while pit emptied loosing zero dump time as the pit was about empty when dumping the next wet truck. Markets rallied a few weeks back on Brazil weather then sold off on same and now climbing on better demand. Buyers do realize a cheap price. US corn is competitive and front end gulf basis has reacted to it. IE spreads narrowed as river basis rises. Remember spreads say a lot about cash demand and supply! PNW booked tight for the fall and most selling into JFM were freight can be had. Buyers responding as well. Selling winter basis is a solid plan to match cash needs. there is a basis carry and our elevation is busy so will be needing to stay with sales vs delivery month. The JFM we have been buying is equal amounts per month to get a avg price not a delivery window.

Futures continue to drift lower on strong yields being reported and better world weather. With bean and corn harvest going so quick it is over running freight( currently trading 1700/car) which is creating a back log in the country. We have a plan but will take two weeks or a little longer to complete. It is two trains of which one is 142 car for corn, two big bins, a few smaller bins and three ground piles. We will likely be closed for corn at Honeyford Thursday to load a bean train and dry corn only Friday and sat morning until we get a big tank flipped beans to corn. Look to lock in basis for JFM as the backlog will last until winter.

We have been talking and advising selling the carry on rallies. There is nothing very bullish today unless SA weather provides. Earning the carry in large carryout markets is hard. Meaning front end price a lot of the time turns into the back end price when we get there. Or something close. I prefer using grain bins to sell cash carries not hold cash grain. Remember Ed Usset program on building a price. Ron Olson VP General Mills always schooled us in the market is talking. Are we listening??? He also said the price bathtub always equalizes. Just a couple things that stuck with me. We look at export basis/ domestic demand every day vs futures and carries to decide on a plan for space. I would highly advise you do the same as long term price building. Anything you need is these areas contact Wade or myself to make a plan.

Upper tier rains are now enough to finish the row crops. Weather looks good and ending stocks building on all crops. Markets are on the hunt for business and were is that price? Issue is we drop and so do others. Other countries have a much lower standard of living and production costs less so they likely can hold out here longer. We talked about seasonally it bottoms the end of June but also it now is getting help from a ridge building in US allowing hot dry to make its way all the way to western Canada.This will also dry us out and bring needed heat. This week selling off continued as managed money sold wheat and beans to the short side with corn flat. Fundamentals on wheat were North America weather, India announcing little imports, Ukraine raising crop est and harvest. Basis levels were mostly unchanged. Spreads did widen as 2023 crop gets dumped and sold against the July making room for the new crop. Once again the avg in sales has worked ( bird in the hand thing) as most spring rallies fail. Basis wise it was quiet this week on all crops. All are a bit on the weak side but commercial is mostly handling it. Futures in wheat and corn were weak as they see planting windows. Now its next weeks planting progress late Monday and weather that will move the market. If long range weather forecasts are correct May stays wet and then turns dryer in June. Western Canada would suffer from this as moisture would not flow that far north. Now gulf moisture is making its way to Canada as well. Would great for us as we have subsoil and with normal rains there is real possibilities yield wise. As always if you get undersold or oversold short date cheap options are the way to go. Marketing is all about building a price not trying to extract it via getting a extra few cents at time of sale. It may make you feel like you won but the true win is when you sell carry and rallies. Then taking a wait approach to setting the basis. We are here to assist in pointing out opportunities and making plans. Bins are built to earn money and is best if carrying sold grain for the carry.

Taran Langland 

Grew up in Enderlin, ND and moved to Grand Forks after college where I my married my wife, who is from the Fordville area. We have a 2.5 year old daughter, another baby due in May, and a 3 year old Golden Retriever. My background in Ag is with a seed company as a territory manager and in the digital ag space as a field technology specialist. I’m excited to work for Honeyford Famers Elevator and I look forward to working with you and making your operation as successful as possible.


Max Schlosser.

I grew up in central North Dakota just about my whole life, more specifically in Rugby. My father was an agronomist, and my mother’s side of the family farmed near my hometown. I have always enjoyed agriculture as well as everything else outdoors, so I went on to study agronomy at Bismarck State College. After my first year their; I spent my spring and summer as an intern with an agronomy center close to home. I then went on to finish college up this past year. I am now here very eager to meet and work with all of the local farmers in the area.

This is why we are sellers when futures outrun basis. Its a sign we left demand in the review mirror. We should start to see extra demand but China is one to watch as their economy is not doing well. Report day is the 12th and history has this one a market mover. We have posted recently defending 8 dollar wheat and actually if behind on sales of corn and beans buy short date puts or sell more cash or both. last report we bought short date puts and it rallied and gave us a selling opportunity but lost some on puts. That's ok and what the move is designed to do. Rule of thumb is sell balance of old crop wheat by May 12th, Corn by July 1st and beans late July mid August. But this year we have the inverses to contend with so it's harder.


Morning weather looks like less rain and warm and dry after this weekend giving the north country time to plant most if not all of its crops. Soil if in great shape and subsoil best in aa while. This should get plants out of the ground and growing in a hurry saving its vigor.


World markets are cheaper than US so we do have downside potential. Bean demand is down from China and Brazil has a big crop. Corn same. Wheat its Australia, Canada and Black Sea.


Long term its weather and Russia/Ukraine as what if's.
